page: Amazon Web Services x2iezn.metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server powered by an Intel Xeon 8252C processor. It features 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a high clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing a high resource density of 32.0 GB of RAM per physical core. It does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage with a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Benchmark data highlights strong memory performance, with uncached large-block read bandwidth reaching 210.08 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 98.02 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25% of tested systems. Single-threaded gzip compression is also highly efficient at 31.99 GB/sec. CPU-heavy tasks show average performance, with a Passmark CPU score of 49425.07 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 13676.0. However, software compilation with Clang performs strongly, scoring 39257.0.

While the server excels in memory-intensive operations and high-speed network throughput, it exhibits performance limitations in specific workloads. LLM text generation speeds are weak to poor, with the medium 7B model achieving only 7.8 tokens/sec. Given the massive 1.5 TB memory capacity, 100 Gbps network baseline, and high-frequency dedicated cores, this bare-metal instance is best suited for large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise applications, memory-intensive data processing, and high-throughput network workloads rather than LLM text generation.

It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8252C processor with 48 vCPUs running at 4.5 GHz, paired with 1536.0 GB of DDR4 memory. The instance lacks local storage and GPUs, but delivers a high baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps. Benchmark results demonstrate strong memory performance, with uncached large-block read bandwidth reaching 210.08 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 98.02 GB/sec. While software compilation and data compression perform in the top tier, LLM text generation speeds are weak, making this server less suitable for real-time AI generation. Instead, its massive memory footprint and high-frequency cores make it highly efficient for in-memory databases, large-scale caching layers, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
